Legal texts require a formal tone to convey authority and precision. Formal adjectives help set this register by replacing everyday terms with words that sound more precise and professional. Notice how the choice of adjectives (and other vocabulary) changes the tone:
"The corporation is required to comply with the applicable regulations."
) not only elevate the text’s tone but also ensure the meaning is precise and unambiguous—a crucial requirement in legal documents.

The Legal Systems: Common Law and Civil Law
The world’s legal systems can be divided into two main categories:

originated in England and is used in countries such as the United States, Canada, and Australia. It is based on judicial decisions, meaning that courts rely on precedents from previous cases. Judges have more flexibility in interpreting the law.
is the legal system in countries like Brazil, Germany, and France. It is based on written codes and statutes, meaning that judges apply the law strictly according to the legal text.
, a judge may decide a case based on how similar cases were ruled in the past. In contrast, in
, the judge will apply a written rule from the legal code—even if a similar case was decided differently before.
As a result, legal professionals working with international law must understand these differences when translating documents or interpreting legal texts.
